Houston County Commissioners Meeting
                            September 22, 2026
                          Warner Robins, Georgia
The Houston County Board of Commissioners met in a Regular Session at 5:00 p.m. on
Wednesday, September 22, 2026, at the Houston County Annex in Warner Robins, Georgia.
Chairman Perdue presided, and Commissioners Byrd, Gottwals, Robinson, and Talton were
present. Director of Administration Robbie Dunbar, Director of Operations Brian Jones, and
County Attorney Tom Hall were also present.

Chairman Perdue gave the invocation.

Commissioner Robinson led those in attendance in the Pledge of Allegiance.

Chairman Perdue presented a proclamation to Angela Anderson and Charmain Josette Curtis,
Organizing Leader of the 100 Black Women, Inc. of Middle Georgia, recognizing October 3,
2026, as National Coalition of 100 Black Women, Inc., Middle Georgia Chapter Recognition
Day.

Ms. Curtis commented on the core values, purpose, and goals of the 100 Black Women, Inc. of
Middle Georgia.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
meeting minutes from the September 1, 2026, and September 9, 2026, Board meetings.

Director of Administration Robbie Dunbar gave the first reading for the alcohol license
application of Rock N Roll Liquors, located at 10130 GA Hwy. 247 N., Suite 100, Warner
Robins. A second reading and public hearing on this application will take place at the Tuesday,
October 6, 2026, Commissioners meeting.

Chairman Perdue explained that County ordinances regarding the approval of liquor store
applications have recently changed, but this application was already underway before the
ordinance change took effect, so it was allowed to proceed under the old ordinance.

Ms. Robinson presented a request from the City of Perry for annexation of property located at
2011 Hwy 41 and Perry Parkway.

Chairman Perdue opened the floor for Public Comments on this annexation.

There being no comments, the meeting continued.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Talton, and carried unanimously by all to concur with
the City of Perry’s request for annexation of 45.69 +/- acres located at 2011 Hwy 41 and Perry
Parkway, also known as Tax Parcels #000310 040000, #000310 021000, #000310 039000, and
#000310 023000. Current zoning is County R-AG and County C-2, proposed zoning is City of
Perry C-2.

Ms. Robinson presented a request from the City of Perry for annexation of property located on
Hicks Drive.

Chairman Perdue opened the floor for Public Comments on this annexation.

There being no comments, the meeting continued.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to concur with
the City of Perry’s request for annexation of 6.61 acres located on Hicks Drive, also known as
Tax Parcels #000340 003000 and #000340 011000. Current zoning is County M-1, proposed
zoning is City of Perry C-2.




               Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 2

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 1


Ms. Robinson presented a request from the City of Warner Robins for annexation of property
located at 747 Elberta Road.

Chairman Perdue opened the floor for Public Comments on this annexation.

There being no comments, the meeting continued.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to concur
with the City of Warner Robins’ request for annexation of 0.508 acres located at 747 Elberta
Road, being a portion of Tax Parcel #000960 039000. Current zoning is County C-1, proposed
zoning is City of Warner Robins C-1.

Ms. Robinson presented a request from Mr. John Rowlands, Race Director of the 17th Annual
“Run 2 End Alzheimer’s at the Landings,” for approval of a race on Saturday, April 3, 2027.

Motion by Ms. Robinson, second by Mr. Talton, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
use of county roads for the upcoming Annual “Run 2 End Alzheimer’s at the Landings” to
benefit the Georgia Alzheimer’s Association. This event will take place on Saturday, April 3,
2027. The Landing Pointe Plaza in Bonaire will serve as both the start and finish for the 5K and
10K runs. Mr. Rowlands has requested Sheriff’s Office assistance with traffic control.

Chairman Perdue invited race director John Rowlands to make comments about the race.

Mr. Rowlands expressed his appreciation to Chairman Perdue, the Commissioners, Sheriff
Moulton and his deputies for their approval of the race and assistance with traffic and road
closures during the event. He stated that the number of participants would be capped at 500 and
that organizers are looking to raise more than $60,000 to help fund research into a cure for
Alzheimer’s.

Chairman Perdue thanked Mr. Rowlands for his efforts in planning the race and raising money
toward finding a cure for the disease. He also thanked Sheriff Moulton and the deputies in his
department for their help and involvement in keeping the runners safe during the event.

Mr. Gottwals presented a request from the Public Defender’s Office for a Secondary
Independent Contractor Agreement to provide legal representation to indigent defendants.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
signing a Secondary Independent Contractor Agreement with Paige Mackenzie Miller for a term
starting on October 5, 2026, and ending on June 30, 2027, for a total of $32,400, paid at $3,600
per month for the first 60 hours and $65 per hour for hours beyond 60 each month.

Mr. Gottwals presented a request from the Board of Elections for approval of hiring poll
workers, and renting equipment, for the November 3, 2026 General Election.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve hiring
the following poll workers, and renting the following equipment for the November 3, 2026,
General Election:

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
rescission of the 2016 infrastructure agreement with the City of Warner Robins effective 60
days from today.

Mr. Byrd commented that, between local governments, it is critical to have a spirit of
cooperation and that this plan is focused on giving fair and equitable treatment to existing water
customers in the County, those on the other side of transition meters, and members of the
development community who invest in and expand these water systems. He concluded by saying
he was optimistic about progress toward a new IGA on this subject soon.

Chairman Perdue stated that an updated infrastructure agreement had been sought for over a
year without success and that the County was continuing discussions with the City of Warner
Robins. He stated he was optimistic that progress would continue toward an agreement. He
stated that higher connection fees ensure that the expense of capital expansion is paid by new
users, that better County oversight is needed regarding what happens on the other side of
transition meters, and that he hopes an agreement can be reached soon. He concluded by saying
that the County would continue to provide service to existing customers and serve others as
County water customers if needed.

Mr. Talton presented a request to enter into a project agreement with the Georgia Department
of Natural Resources.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
Chairman Perdue signing a project agreement with the Georgia Department of Natural
Resources for a total project cost of $3,382,700, with Georgia Outdoor Stewardship Program
(GOSP) funds of $2,340,000 and County funds or in-kind participation of $1,042,700. The
project period may not exceed 24 months from the date of signing.

Chairman Perdue thanked the Commissioners for their support of this project and said that this
park, on the northern border of Houston County, would be a nice addition to the County and
provide a place for fishing, a kayak and canoe launch, walking trails, and other amenities for
Houston County residents.

Mr. Talton presented a request from Public Works for approval of bids on equipment.




                Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 4

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 3


Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
following bids on equipment for Public Works:

Chairman Perdue thanked the citizens of Houston County for their continued support of
SPLOST and noted that the County was still spending from the 2018 SPLOST. He also thanked
Public Works staff and the Roads and Bridges Department for their wise use of these funds. He
also thanked Roads and Bridges Superintendent Travis McClendon for his effective work and
leadership within his department. He concluded by stating that this tree trimmer would allow
the County to perform this work internally, which had previously been contracted out.

Mr. Talton presented a request from the Sheriff’s Office to approve bids on various vehicles,
including a revised price for the Warrants Division truck approved at the August 4, 2026,
Commissioners Meeting.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Mr. Byrd, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
following bids on vehicles to be used in multiple divisions of the Sheriff’s Office:

Chairman Perdue thanked Sheriff Moulton for his wise budget management.

Mr. Talton presented a request from Public Works to enter into a contract to construct the SR
127 Water Supply & Treatment Facility.

Motion by Mr. Talton, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
entering into a contract with Parrish Construction Group, of Perry, Georgia, with a Guaranteed
Maximum Price of $11,428,520.71 to construct the SR 127 Water Supply & Treatment Facility.
This project will be funded by Water Capital Funds and has a contract time of 570 days. County
consulting engineers Carter & Sloope, Inc., recommend approval of this contract.



               Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 5

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 4


Mr. Byrd expressed his appreciation to everyone involved who helped get the project to this
point and said he was appreciative that the system would allow for the funding of capital
improvements using existing funds.

Chairman Perdue agreed and expressed his appreciation to Carter and Sloope, who helped the
County with this project, and to Parrish Construction for doing a great job on the GMP for the
project and coming in under budget. He also thanked Utilities Superintendent Terry Dietsch,
Director of Operations Brian Jones, and multiple other departments for their help and assistance
to date. Chairman Perdue also stated that, with the County’s current rate structure and tap fees
on new accounts, this project is expected to be paid for with future revenue and cash on hand.

Director of Administration Robbie Dunbar stated that the project should be funded using the
County’s current water fund reserves and surplus, and that it would continue to be monitored.

Mr. Byrd presented a request from Public Works for approval to replace the HVAC units at the
Public Works Administrative Building.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
bid from Wilson Bryant Air Conditioning of Macon, Georgia, in the amount of $69,985 to
replace three HVAC units at the Public Works Administrative Building. This item is in the
current-year budget and will be funded by the 2018 SPLOST. Equipment lead time is
approximately two months, and installation will be completed within one month of arrival.

Mr. Byrd requested approval of the final closeout adjustment to the American Rescue Plan Act
(ARPA) Fiscal Recovery Fund. All funds must be expended by December 31, 2026, and
closeout reporting sent to the U.S. Treasury.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Talton, and carried unanimously by all to approve the final
ARPA project budget adjustments shown below, and authorize the Accounting Department to
file the final U.S. Treasury closeout reports, with any final adjustments to be ratified by the
Board:

Chairman Perdue thanked Accounting, Public Works, and MIS staff for their help and
involvement, along with Director of Administration Robbie Dunbar, and Community Planner
Jake Cox, on the ARPA projects and quarterly submissions. He stated that he had a goal of not
sending any ARPA grant money back to the federal government, but that it looks like under
$100,000 out of the $30 million ARPA grant the County received could possibly be returned,
which he considered an accomplishment in itself.

Mr. Byrd presented a request to approve an Intergovernmental Agreement with the City of Perry
that replaces the prior infrastructure agreements.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Ms. Robinson and carried unanimously by all to approve
entering into an Infrastructure Intergovernmental Agreement with the City of Perry establishing
updated standards for transition meters, County infrastructure, and water connection fees.


                Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 6

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 5


Chairman Perdue thanked the City of Perry for its work in securing the language it would like
included in this agreement and for the City already collecting water fees on its side of the
transition meter, which allows the County to fund expansion to the County’s water system.

Mr. Byrd presented a request from the Sheriff’s Office for approval to donate a 2012 Ford
Econoline van that has reached the end of its service life and has been replaced.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Mr. Gottwals, and carried unanimously by all to approve the
donation of one 2012 Ford Econoline van to the Peach County Sheriff’s Office.

Motion by Mr. Byrd, second by Ms. Robinson and carried unanimously by all to approve the
payment of the bills totaling $4,979,125.92.

Chairman Perdue opened the floor for Public Comments.

Ernie and Sandra Walker spoke about the abandonment of right-of-way along their road,
inquiring about the notice of abandonment, the relocation of water meters, and other concerns.

Chairman Perdue stated he would get answers to all their questions and get in contact with them.

Jeff Summers, Southfield Plantation Homeowners Association President, spoke about the
development at the back of the subdivision. He asked about a second entrance for the new
development. He then asked about the Thompson Mill Road extension and expressed concern
about use by tractor-trailers.

Chairman Perdue stated that, if necessary, he would look into making it a no-thru truck route.

There being no further comments, Chairman Perdue closed Public Comments and opened
Commissioner Comments.

Mr. Gottwals spoke about the recent passing of author Annie Dillard and gave a quote from her:
“No one escapes walking through the wilderness to reach the promised land.” He concluded by
thanking everyone for attending.

Ms. Robinson thanked everyone for coming to the meeting and commented positively about the
final ARPA budget returning less than $100,000. She said she was proud of the County
employees and all public safety personnel.

Mr. Talton thanked everyone for attending the meeting, recognized the United States Air Force
on its 79th birthday, held on September 17. He concluded by expressing his appreciation to
Laura Mathis, Greg Boike, and the other staff with the Middle Georgia Regional Commission
for their assistance in helping the Board cast a vision for the future of Houston County through
recent planning sessions for an updated Comprehensive Plan.

Mr. Byrd thanked everyone for attending the evening’s meeting and recognized Warner Robins
Councilman Larry Curtis for attending. Commissioner Byrd concluded his comments by
recognizing the passing of two well-known Houston County residents, Draper Watson of
Watson-Hunt Funeral Home and Sam Buzzell, owner of Buzzell Plumbing and Heating and Air.

Mr. Byrd read an excerpt from Mr. Watson’s obituary “He invested his life in its people, its
institutions, and its future. Generation after generation of Perry families knew him through the
Watson-Hunt name, but more importantly, they knew Draper – the man who showed up at any
time of the day or night, answered the phone, shook their hand, sat with them in difficult times,
celebrated their joys, and treated their families as if they were his own – carrying forward the
legacy entrusted to him. His legacy will live on, not only through his family and Watson-Hunt,
but through the countless people whose lives he touched along the way.” He then commented
that Mr. Watson served on the Development Authority of Houston County.



                Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued on Page 7

Houston County Commissioners Meeting Continued from Page 6


Mr. Byrd read an excerpt from Mr. Buzzell’s obituary “Samuel was patient, kind, fiercely loyal,
and generous to a fault. He worked hard throughout his life, but he also understood the
importance of making time for family, friends, and the things he loved. His life was marked not
only by the businesses he built or the positions he held, but by the relationships he nurtured, the
lessons he passed down, and the many lives made better by knowing him.” He then commented
that Mr. Buzzell served as a Houston County Commissioner.

Chairman Perdue thanked the Board for the accomplishments at the meeting and commented
that he spent the day at a regional water council meeting in Atlanta. He noted that much of the
evening’s agenda reflected work regarding water and that Houston County is blessed to have
access to the aquifer and water resources it has. He said the County will work to manage this
resource in the best way possible. Chairman Perdue closed his comments by also reflecting on
the comments made by Mr. Byrd about Mr. Watson and Mr. Buzzell.

Motion by Mr. Gottwals, second by Ms. Robinson, and carried unanimously by all to approve
adjourning the meeting. Meeting adjourned.
